solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tailless little bird taps shallow drinking vessel

indicators.note: a creature without a tail loses its end, so the bird's word drops its final letter

parts.note: a quail is a small game bird
C and H are the letters on the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: A small bird with no tail pecks at a shallow cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' cuts the last letter from QUAIL. A quaich is a traditional Scottish two-handled cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaich is a shallow two-handled Scottish cup used for toasts, so it is a drinking vessel of that kind.

clue.text: Reckoned copper has entered name and date incorrectly

indicators.note: one thing entering another means it goes inside it, so copper's symbol sits within the word for name

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: written incorrectly, the letters of date come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A police officer has written down a name and date wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element Cu. 'Incorrectly' rearranges DATE as ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculated is a past-tense verb meaning worked out by arithmetic, the same as reckoned.

clue.text: Moving slowly, old man being fed by wife Heather

indicators.note: something fed by another takes it in, so the father word swallows the letter for wife

parts.note: old man is informal for one's father, dad
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Dad shuffles along slowly while his wife Heather feeds him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like the wife's name, but it is the plant, ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling means lingering or going slowly, so it describes moving at a slow pace.

clue.text: Exact definition of "offer" initiated new term for "suggestion"

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of the two quoted words are put in a fresh order
a term is an end or limit, so it points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dictionary gives a precise definition, offering a new term for suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges OFFER INITIATED; 'term for' takes N, the end of suggestion. 'Term' looks like a word but means an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Differentiation is the act of telling things apart precisely, which is what an exact definition does.

clue.text: Snapper on line getting no space?

definitions.text: Snapper on line getting no space?

parts.words: Snapper on line getting no space?
parts.note: a camera on the web: the two words run together with no space between them make the name of the device

explanation.surface: A photographer working online finds no room to work.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'snapper' is a camera, 'on line' puts it on the web, and 'no space' tells you to write the two words as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcam is a small camera that sends its pictures over the internet, a snapper working online.

clue.text: Partly overturned degeneracy charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the picked run is read from bottom to top
only part of the word degeneracy is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A charge of moral decay has been partly overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' picks ERAC from inside degenERACy and 'overturned' turns it round. 'Charge' looks like a legal accusation but means responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone in your care is to have them as your charge, under your responsibility.

clue.text: Shakespearean character worked out crime

indicators.note: worked in the sense of kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A character from Shakespeare has solved the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' reads as solved, but 'worked' rearranges OUT and CRIME together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercutio is Romeo's witty friend in Romeo and Juliet, killed by Tybalt, a Shakespeare character.

clue.text: I see you can set back a language

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: ta-ra is a northern English way of saying goodbye, like see you
a jug is a container, a can in the loose sense of vessel

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a can while saying goodbye in a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set back' reverses I + TARA + JUG. 'Ta-ra' is informal British slang for goodbye, much like 'see you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarati is the Indo-Aryan language of the Indian state of Gujarat, so it is one language among many.

clue.text: Empire's last Dark Lord, one effecting escape

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here taken from the empire's name

parts.note: Darth Vader is the Dark Lord of the Sith in Star Wars

explanation.surface: A Star Wars line: the Empire's final Sith Lord makes a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empire' and 'Dark Lord' set a Star Wars scene; the Empire's last letter is E.
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is someone who dodges or escapes, so one effecting escape fits as a noun.

clue.text: Metal swizzle stick once seen centrally

indicators.note: centrally means the letters at the centre of each of the three words are picked out

explanation.surface: A metal swizzle stick is something you might once have seen at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres of swiZzle, stIck and oNCe give Z, I and NC; the even-length 'once' gives its two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic element, used for galvanising iron.

clue.text: Shortage that is stopping cynic getting fed bananas

indicators.note: stopping as a plug or stopper, so the abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A shortage of food stops a cynic from being fed bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit the cynic is fed, but it is slang for crazy and signals the rearrangement; 'stopping' means plugging, a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficiency is a lack or insufficiency of something, which is a shortage.

clue.text: Foreign character sick over hot dish

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for sick is written backwards

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A foreign person becomes ill after eating a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' looks like a person but is the Greek letter CHI. 'Over' reverses ILL to LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli, short for chilli con carne, is a spicy stew, and hot describes its peppery heat.

clue.text: Traces martens back to Eurasian ground

indicators.note: ground as in milled or crushed, so the letters are broken and rearranged
the back of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone traces martens, the weasel-like animals, back to their Eurasian homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to Eurasian' gives its last letter N, and 'ground' mixes it with MARTENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Remnants are small remaining pieces or vestiges, the same as traces left behind.

clue.text: News time for some day workers, maybe those who wait on

parts.note: the BBC's News at Ten gives the time at ten
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: For some people who work days, news time comes too late.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'News at Ten' is a long-running British evening news bulletin, so the news time is AT TEN. Ants are the standard workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendants are servants or helpers whose job is to serve and assist, waiting on others.

clue.text: The effing stupid allowance concerning future IT?

indicators.note: stupid as in muddled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or goods

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a stupid allowance meant for future technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' rearranges THE EFFING into FIFTHGENE, then RATION is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifth-generation computing was the 1980s label for the next wave of computers built on AI and parallel processing.

clue.text: Monk supposes said year will be terrible

indicators.note: something terrible here is mangled, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A monk predicts that the year just named will be a terrible one.
explanation.walkthrough: Monk is this puzzle's setter, so 'Monk' stands for I. 'Will be terrible' rearranges SAID YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: When the setter Monk supposes something, in his own voice he says I dare say, a phrase of assumption.

clue.text: Fish in 50% of dishes after starters of roll and soup

indicators.note: after places the half-word behind the three initials
starters are the openers, so the first letter of each of the three words is taken
50% of a word is its first half, here of a ten-letter word for dishes

parts.note: casseroles are oven dishes, both the pot and the stew

explanation.surface: A fish served in half a casserole after a roll and soup to start.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' takes the first half of the ten-letter word for the dishes; 'after' puts that behind the initials given by 'starters of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascasse is the scorpion fish, a classic ingredient of bouillabaisse in Provence.

clue.text: Cross over to enter function with international food

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the turned word goes into the other letters

parts.note: tan is short for tangent, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for cross is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix

explanation.surface: Someone crosses over to an event that has international food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party but is the tangent from trigonometry. 'Over' turns the cross round into DOOR, which 'to enter' places before the final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori dishes are Indian food baked in a clay oven called a tandoor.

clue.text: Hold old trophy in, ultimately, Pyrrhic victory

indicators.note: in puts the trophy inside the two final letters
ultimately means at the last, so the last letter of each word is taken

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: An old trophy is held after a Pyrrhic victory, won at too great a cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes C and Y from Pyrrhic and victory; 'in' places CUP between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a place or post is to hold it, as an army holds ground.

clue.text: Rules charge should follow offence in hearing?

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard, so what follows is said aloud and matched to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sin is an offence and a tax is a charge, the tax coming after the sin

explanation.surface: At a court hearing, a penalty follows the offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hearing' looks like a court hearing but means the pieces are said aloud: sin + tax sounds like the grammar word.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the set of grammatical rules for arranging words into sentences.

clue.text: Band finally together in East-End group of houses?

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the shortened village word
East End Cockneys drop their aitches, so the H is cut

parts.note: a hamlet is a small group of houses, a tiny village

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word together

explanation.surface: A band that finally gets together in a small East End village.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End Cockney accent drops initial H, so HAMLET becomes 'AMLET; 'finally' takes R from together and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band or bracelet worn round the upper arm.

clue.text: Too much in rat race, orderly that's fired

indicators.note: in puts the excess abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
put in order, the letters are rearranged into a new, tidy sequence

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Someone in the rat race who is too orderly gets fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests sacked, but means baked in a kiln. 'Orderly' rearranges RAT RACE as TERRACA and 'in' puts OTT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed earthenware baked hard in a kiln, so it is clay that has been fired.

clue.text: Danger of search lacking force

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter for force is removed

parts.note: to frisk is to search someone by patting them
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: There is danger in a search done without using force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops F from FRISK.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a hazard or chance of harm, the same as a danger.

clue.text: Host owning many branches?

definitions.meaning: a host is a great multitude
read as arm-y, having many arms like a branching tree

explanation.surface: A host who owns many branches of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense coins an adjective from arm with -y, like branchy.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a host in the old sense of a large body of soldiers, and arm-y jokingly means full of limbs.

clue.text: Renounce exam success at college

parts.note: a pass is success in an exam
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student gives up a hard-won exam pass at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, being 'up' means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to decline or forgo it, giving it up.

clue.text: Assailant formerly working with yours truly?

parts.note: on means functioning or working, as a machine is on
the setter is the crossword compiler, who refers to himself as yours truly

explanation.surface: A former attacker now working alongside me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the compiler, the SETTER. 'Formerly' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Onsetter is an old word for an attacker, from onset meaning an assault.
